name: Zelophehad
overview: Zelophehad was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, known uniquely as the son of Hepher who had only daughters. This detail highlights a particular family circumstance recorded in Numbers 26:33. There are no additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zelophehad means 'shadow of dread' or 'terror,' which can also be understood as 'protection from terror or dread.' This proper name, not indicated as given by God, reflects a significant Hebrew meaning that may imply divine protection or a formidable presence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zelophehad as the son of Hepher. He is also inferred to be the father of Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah, indicating he had only daughters. These relationships are all referenced in Numbers 26:33.
scriptureSignificance: Zelophehad is significant in the biblical narrative primarily because of his unique family situation as a man with only daughters, which posed a challenge to inheritance laws in Israel. His case is recorded to highlight issues of inheritance rights within the tribe of Manasseh. This serves as a foundation for understanding God's provision and justice in the distribution of land among His people.
